how_to_fill: Every number in this file and in evals/report-weeks.csv belongs to Brightdesk, the made-up example company: replace them all with your own. Write the questions your team actually asks, in their words. For each one put the number your team already trusts for that week (from the weekly report, not from the catalog) and the metric that should answer it. If step 5 found a difference between the metric and the report and the report's owner accepted the metric's number, put the metric's number here, and keep the report's number and the cause in "report" and "why" (q03 shows how). Keep at least one trap (two metrics with similar names), one number that lives outside PostHog, and one number the catalog does not have. Re-check the expected numbers when the weeks get old: a late refund or a deleted account changes history.

questions.question: How many new paying customers did we get in the week starting 12 October 2026?
How many seats did new customers buy in the week of 5 October 2026?
How many people visited our website in the week starting 28 September 2026?
questions.why: The report takes visitors from the Web analytics page, which puts a visitor in the week the session started; the metric uses the pageview time. Owner accepted the metric's number.
